paper_title: Investigating the gamma-ray burst from decaying MeV-scale axion-like particles produced in supernova explosions
coupling_convention: g_agamma in GeV^-1, canonical axion-photon coupling
notes: Paper presents a revised and strengthened bound on the axion-photon coupling g_agamma from SN 1987A gamma-ray observations by the Solar Maximum Mission (SMM). The key improvement over prior work is the inclusion of photon coalescence production mechanism for heavy ALPs (m_a > 70 MeV), which extends the exclusion bound from ~200 MeV to ~280 MeV. The bound is derived at 3-sigma confidence level from the non-observation of a gamma-ray burst in the 25-100 MeV range within 223 seconds after the neutrino burst. The paper also provides a Fermi-LAT sensitivity projection (dashed red line in Fig. 3) for a future nearby SN, which would improve the bound by ~1 order of magnitude in coupling and extend to ~2x larger masses. The mass-independent bound is encoded as a horizontal line spanning the validity range (10 keV to 280 MeV). The boundary shows a characteristic rise with mass, consistent with the photon coalescence production mechanism becoming more efficient at higher ALP masses. The black dashed line represents the SN 1987A bound from Ref. [19], and the red dashed contours show Case 1 and Case 2 sensitivity estimates.
